body.statement: Theorem 1. The functional \(w\mapsto\sup_{b\in\mathcal B_H}\operatorname{Var}_{Z_H}S_H(w,b;Z_H)\) is coercive on \(\mathcal W_H\): for the Euclidean norm on the \(m_H\) attainable-support coordinates, its value diverges whenever \(\|w\|_2\to\infty\) with \(w\in\mathcal W_H\). Primal and dual optimizers exist and \[v_H=\min_{w\in\mathcal W_H}\max_{b\in\mathcal B_H}\operatorname{Var}_{Z_H}S_H(w,b;Z_H)=\max_{\Pi\in\mathcal P(\mathcal B_H)}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_H}\int_{\mathcal B_H}\operatorname{Var}_{Z_H}S_H(w,b;Z_H)\,d\Pi(b)=D_H.\] Moreover, \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=v_H/(rh^2)\), and \(\mathfrak P_H\) has optimal value \(v_H\). A feasible \(w^*\) minimizes if and only if an attained \(\Pi^*\), supported on its variance contact set, makes the integrated variance gradient orthogonal to the tangent space of \(\mathcal W_H\).
body.justification: Attainment and contacts make the scale graph-computable and characterize every optimal weight.
body.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026, arXiv version 2, Section 4 and Appendix B fix one feasible Bernoulli quadratic weight, while Proposition 4.1 gives an MSE envelope from the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4. None gives the attained repeated-motif conditional-variance constant, its robust program, or its integral-of-conditional-variance dual.
body.consumer: In the LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network experiments of PougetAbadieEtAl2019, the known repeated local graph motif determines which feasible exposure-quadratic weight minimizes the worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant; that motif-level choice sets the exact test threshold and power calibration relative to deploying the fixed GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 weight.
